reasons.order: Opens with the compiler and its executor/service wiring (`SqlPlanCompiler`, `QueryPlan.SqlStep`, `resolveQueryExecutorMode`, `hasCompleteSnapshots`) and only then moves to the index-schema consequences, client comparator alignment and benchmarks/doc, so the core lands first even if the `parentId`/`propPathNormalized` migrations would read slightly better before the tests chapter.
reasons.why: Prose repeatedly supplies the constraint rather than narrating: `INDEXED BY`/`NOT INDEXED` exist because SQLite without `ANALYZE` rates a `queueId` equality as cheap as `(spaceId, objectId)`, `localEntityId` returns null cross-space because ids can collide after a join, and `buildTypeDxnCondition`'s range exists because `= OR LIKE` cannot seek.
reasons.load: Each chapter introduces its terms before use (mode resolution before `#execCompiled`, `planReadsObjectMeta` before the fallback), though the tests chapter points back to "the earlier benchmark chapter" that actually appears last.
reasons.trust: Numbers and symbols check out (17× traversal regression, `idx_object_index_queueObjectId` pin, 200 differential rounds), but the client chapter calls `WorkingSetQueryExecutor` "the client-side fallback path that runs when a query can't be ... evaluated by the SQL engine on the host", which the patch and design doc contradict — it is the optimistic local layer.

reasons.order: The compiler leads, which is right, but the executor/service wiring that makes it reachable (`QueryPlan.SqlStep`, `resolveQueryExecutorMode`, `#execCompiled`) is deferred two chapters behind the schema work, forcing the compiler chapter to promise "covered in the pipeline wiring chapter".
reasons.why: Names the load-bearing reasons explicitly: `planReadsObjectMeta` declines because `objectSnapshot` strips `@meta`, the index hints are a deliberate override of a planner with no `ANALYZE` statistics, and the `localEntityId` null is to stop cross-space id collisions after a join.
reasons.load: The entire 1,513-line `compile.ts` block is emitted twice — once for the class overview and again for "predicate compilation" — so a reviewer scrolls the same file body a second time before reaching the tests.
reasons.trust: Most claims verify, but the client chapter describes `WorkingSetQueryExecutor` as "the in-memory (host) executor used as the baseline for comparison tests" when it lives in `echo-client/src/query/`, and it places the `hasCompleteSnapshots`/`countMissingSnapshots` pair together on `ObjectSnapshotIndex` when the former is on `IndexEngine`.

reasons.order: The opening declares that "the compiler itself (`echo-host/src/query/sql/compile.ts`) and its wiring into the executor are covered elsewhere", so the core of the change is pushed into the 58-hunk "Also changed" dump and the document sequences only prerequisites.
reasons.why: Good constraint-level reasoning inside its scope — `parent`/`source`/`target` hold full EID strings so a join needs concatenation the `(spaceId, objectId)` index cannot serve; trigram terms under three characters fall back to `LIKE` and cannot rank — but the title's "behind a flag" is never explained and `DX_ECHO_QUERY_EXECUTOR` never appears.
reasons.load: Individually the sections are short and clear, yet a reviewer who has not seen the code is left without the compiler, the mode switch, or the fallback rule that the plan-step and `propPathNormalized` sections exist to serve.
reasons.trust: "The column list the migration test checks picks up all six new columns" is wrong — the `migrations.test.ts` hunk adds three (`parentId`, `sourceId`, `targetId`) — and the fts fence names a malformed path, `packages/core/index-core/../../index-core/src/indexes/fts-index.ts`.
